name: Back terrace
orientation: Open to the sky; walled on three sides, low wall on the fourth with the barbecue area; reached through the new double doors from the kitchen

photos.caption: Looking back at the new kitchen doors: patched render, damp staining at the base, outdoor socket, festoon lights
Seating corner: pallet sofas, old shutters hung on the neighbour's stone wall, small bricked-up opening
Barbecue corner and view to the church and clock tower; gas water heater in the alcove on the right; tarp-covered structure

current.summary: Roof terrace of about 2.5 × 4 m off the kitchen, terracotta tile floor. Walls on three sides: the house wall with the new kitchen doors (render patched around them, green-yellow damp staining at the base, a crenellated/scalloped parapet top), a high rendered wall, and the rough stone wall of the neighbouring building with an old pair of louvred wooden shutters hung on it as decoration and a small bricked-up opening. The fourth side is a low wall with the barbecue area and a view over the roofs to the church and the clock tower. In a covered alcove: a Vaillant gas water heater with loose wiring and a yellow gas hose, an old brown enamel stove, a flexible metal flue duct. A timber structure with roof tiles on top is wrapped in torn tarpaulins. Furniture: L-shaped pallet seating with navy cushions, wooden dining table, wrought-iron bench, festoon lights.
keep: The stone neighbour wall and the hung shutters — great character
The view to the church and clock tower
issues: Gas water heater alcove: loose wiring and exposed gas hose — needs a gas engineer check and a proper cover/cabinet
Torn tarpaulins over the tiled timber structure — what is it? Repair, rebuild as storage, or remove
Damp/algae staining at the base of the house wall — find the cause (splash-back, no drip, poor drainage) before re-rendering
Patched render round the new doors to finish; surface-mounted conduit and socket box
Old stove and duct stored outside

target.concept: DRAFT — an outdoor dining room. Clear the clutter and the tarps, box the water heater into a neat louvred timber cabinet, render and lime-wash the house wall in a warm white, keep the stone wall raw. Replace the pallets with a built-in masonry bench along the stone wall (cushions in outdoor linen), a proper table for four, the barbecue on the low wall side, festoon lights re-hung on a tidy wire, and big terracotta pots with lemon, rosemary and a climbing jasmine.
